dispositions.statement: The filer prints its ratio of net investment income to average net assets for the year to date and says it is not annualised (10-Qs; the 10-K prints the year). The company-facts step splits that running ratio into quarters, so income_yield_pct holds one quarter's unannualised ratio (2.13 to 3.22). F16 compares it, times 1.5, with distribution_rate, which is annualised (four times the quarter's distribution over NAV, 9.7 to 11.9). On one basis the check would not fire in any quarter: four times the quarter's ratio times 1.5 is 12.8 or more against a distribution rate of 11.9 at most. Published equals the page split by quarter; no distribution or income figure is wrong. Fix belongs in the check or in the field's basis across funds (most filers print an annualised ratio, published as filed), which is a shared decision, not this fund's.

addresses_verdict.2025-12-31: The reviewer found the distribution is not excessive (1.96 declared against 1.79 of income a share, NII ratio 9.48 % for the year) and called the F16 value an extraction error. The first half stands; no published figure is wrong: income_yield_pct is the year's 9.48 % less the nine-month 7.17 %, an unannualised quarter, as the filer's running ratio splits. The flag comes from comparing that with an annualised distribution rate, which is this disposition.
